title: How to generate a city
author: Middle_Ad630
selftext:
I am currently building an open world survival game with Godot. The key feature is „realism“, meaning that you can use almost everything and also explore everything.   
The game also features many villages including a main city with over 7.000 buildings you can enter and explore and loot.

Building the city works „okay“ but I’m looking for a way to make it easier and more reliable without me having to look at every street and garden and building to find mistakes while also letting Claude build it automatically. We are currently using OSM for the streets and a zoning and plot generate but it’s not that great. 

Does anyone here maybe have some advice or experience for building that kind of city?

comments.author: VictorBuildsApps
comments.body:
I'd give Claude tools that check the scene data rather than screenshots. In my Blender setup a look check of a render once passed floating trees, so now an audit script is required after a scene change. It lists objects that float above whatever is under them, sink into the ground, or intersect another object, with positions, and groups repeats by the object they copy, so 130 floating copies of one tree would come back as one issue.

For a city the same idea would extend to buildings overlapping each other or sitting off the terrain, reported with a position so Claude can fix them and rerun until the list is empty. You could also check plot footprints against each other in the generator, so overlaps are caught before any building exists. I haven't built city-specific checks, and mine runs in Blender, not Godot, but any engine that lets you query positions and bounds can run the same kind of check.

comments.author: IndianaNetworkAdmin
comments.body:
I'm doing something similar, so I'll tell you how I've done it. Libraries, starting from the smallest object and working my way up.

* Make the individual items/loot that can be found. Classify based on where they could be found and put them into a library.
* Make furniture, add spots for loot/equipment to spawn to the furniture that can be a container, put the furniture+loot nodes into a library.
* Make furniture groups from your furniture, put it into a library. Categorize by room/type. Bedrooms could also be motel/hotel rooms, for example. Living room sets could also go into lounge and waiting areas. Table sets could be restaurants or dining rooms.
* Make rooms, add furniture groups and tertiary furniture spots - For example, you may have a furniture group that's a bed plus end tables, but the dresser goes against a random wall so that's tertiary. Make a room library. Outdoor spaces count as 'rooms' as well, they just have different walls - Either no wall, fences, or a combination.
* You rinse and repeat for building homes, gas stations/convenience stores, etc. For larger buildings, you build them one block at a time and have anchor rooms. A hotel floor would have a lobby and long corridor, and around that would be repeating instances of the same hotel rooms. Only the ground floor with the pool, main lobby, restaurant, and other possible amenities would need special rooms. Office buildings would be similar - You'd have your main entrance at the ground floor with coffee shops or whatever, but everything above that would be nearly identical.

You build your libraries of full buildings by the end, and then you just need to lay out roads and building plots. It looks like you already have a suburb of some kind put together.
